question: Why does the wise person perform bathing and related observances?
premises: The revered Ananda scripture is cited on this point.
For the wise person there is no real impurity.
Bathing and wearing good clothes produce contentment.
inference: For the wise, ritual bathing is not for removing impurity but for generating contentment and fitness.
uncertainties: suvastratvaṃ may refer broadly to clean or proper dress rather than specifically fine garments.
plain_english: And in the revered Ananda scripture it is said that the wise person has no impurity. Rather, bathing and wearing good clothes serve to produce contentment.
